historical_context: Nasreddin Hodja is believed to have lived in 13th century in Aksehir, Seljuk Turkey (1208-1284). Sufi satirist, wise fool, folk philosopher. Stories spread across Ottoman Empire, Persia, Arab world, Central Asia, India. UNESCO declared 1996-1997 International Nasreddin Hodja Year.
note: There are thousands of Nasruddin stories in oral tradition; this file collects 200 most famous, complete versions

stories.title: The Smell of Soup and the Sound of Money
stories.full_story: One day Nasruddin went to a restaurant and saw a man eating soup, inhaling its smell. The restaurant owner demanded money for smelling the soup. Nasruddin stepped in as judge. He took coins from his pocket, jingled them near owner's ear and said: 'The sound of money pays for the smell of soup.'
stories.moral: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
stories.source: Nasreddin Hodja folklore - 13th century, public domain, oral tradition across Turkey, Persia, Central Asia, India
